title: A complex is perfect exactly when it is compact as an object of the derived category

standard_prerequisites.name: The Hom functor out of a bounded above complex of projective modules is computed on the level of complexes, so its cohomology is the cohomology of a product complex
standard_prerequisites.use: Identifies the Hom groups out of the bounded complex of finite projective modules representing a perfect object with the cohomology of a product of Hom modules.

standard_prerequisites.name: A compact object of the derived category has a map to it from a bounded complex of finite free modules which admits a one-sided inverse
standard_prerequisites.use: Produces the finite free complex L, the maps making K a summand of L, and the idempotent endomorphism of L.

core_obligations: Assume K is perfect, represented by a bounded complex P of finite projective modules, and note that a direct sum in the derived category is computed termwise (proof lines 20397-20405).
Replace Hom out of P by the Hom complex and identify its cohomology with a product of Hom modules in each degree, using that the terms of P are projective (proof lines 20406-20420).
Deduce that a map out of K factors through a finite direct sum of the E_i, which is the compactness of K (proof lines 20421-20440).

Conversely take K compact and choose a map from a bounded complex of finite free modules L to K with a one-sided inverse, so that K is a summand of L in the derived category (proof lines 20441-20500).

Use the idempotent endomorphism of L induced by the two maps and the splitting of L into the kernel of the idempotent and the kernel of its complement to write K as a summand of a perfect object, hence as perfect (proof lines 20501-20506).
proof_roadmap: Forward direction: K perfect is represented by a bounded complex of finite projective modules (proof lines 20397-20402).
Compute Hom out of that complex as a product complex and show a map into a direct sum factors through finitely many terms (proof lines 20403-20440).
Backward direction: a compact object receives a map from a bounded complex of finite free modules with a one-sided inverse (proof lines 20441-20470).
Split off the image idempotent, identify K with one of the two summands and conclude with the statement that summands of perfect objects are perfect (proof lines 20471-20506).
difficulty_reason: statement 是两个熟知的等价条件（perfect 即紧对象的刻画），本身是标准结论，不涉及新定义。证明是双向的：正向把 perfect 对象换成有限投射模的有界复形，把 Hom 群算成乘积复形的上同调并由此看出映射只经过有限多个直和项；反向利用紧性得到从有限自由模有界复形出发的带单边逆的映射，再用幂等自同态把该复形劈成两个部分，识别出 K 是其中一个直和项并引用「perfect 的直和项仍 perfect」收尾。真正的演算（乘积复形、直和只经过有限项、幂等分裂）都在 span 内做完，10 处引用里 3 处同章、7 处跨章，全部作导航桩。
